headline: High-risk data leakage and prompt-injection exposure from kotaemon’s broad networked document ingestion into a local-only, non-writing content writer; no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests HTML, MHTML, PDFs, DOCX, and chat transcripts and uses web UI plus API-backed retrieval, so malicious content could be rendered as instructions. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no input channel, so the pairwise bridge is indirect rather than direct. Uncertainty remains about any hidden shared workspace, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF kotaemon content is copied into python-cheatsheet as editable text, injection becomes actionable.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced, attacker-controlled document text can bridge the pair.
mitigations: Restrict kotaemon outputs to plain text summaries.
Disable copy-paste of raw retrieved documents into the writer.
Use a review step that strips instructions from source material.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to retrieved chunks.
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents in separate workspaces.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly touches API keys and broad document classes, while python-cheatsheet is local-only and has no declared data handling. If the writer receives kotaemon outputs containing secrets or sensitive documents, leakage can occur through the pair’s workflow. Because kotaemon has broad network egress and the exact handoff is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF kotaemon processes documents containing secrets or chat transcripts and those outputs are forwarded to python-cheatsheet, leakage occurs.
IF the operator pastes raw kotaemon context into the writer, sensitive data can be exposed.
mitigations: Redact secrets before any handoff.
Keep sensitive documents out of kotaemon.
Use separate accounts and workspaces.
Turn off sharing of raw retrieval context.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on inter-agent transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon can support multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation. There is no documented overlapping mutable surface, so conflict is limited unless an unusual shared directory is configured. The pair is therefore low rather than none because kotaemon’s write surface exists.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps kotaemon’s ./ktem_app_data into a shared workspace, conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Use distinct directories for each agent.
Avoid shared mounts between the two processes.
Run only one kotaemon instance per workspace.
Check for accidental symlinked paths.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces retrieved answers and citations, and python-cheatsheet is a reference-style content writer that could reuse those outputs without verification. No downstream action-taking authority is shown, so this is not high, but the default workflow can still propagate incorrect or manipulated content into published writing. Uncertainty about the handoff warrants medium.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is used to draft text from kotaemon outputs without fact-checking, errors cascade.
IF kotaemon retrieves a false citation and the writer republishes it, the mistake propagates.
mitigations: Require source verification before publication.
Separate drafting from final approval.
Mark retrieved claims as untrusted until checked.
Use a citation audit checklist.
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checking against source documents.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and diverse document classes, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no declared retention or residency controls. If regulated data is processed in kotaemon and then copied into the writer, retention and residency mismatches can arise. The pair lacks explicit compliance controls, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed in kotaemon and transferred into python-cheatsheet, compliance obligations may be duplicated or lost.
IF the operator stores sensitive excerpts in the writer, retention policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the writer.
Minimize retention of copied excerpts.
Document the data flow between tools.
Use separate storage policies per agent.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
